text:
zoe: quick heads-up — onboarding run for sablefish-embed-v1 finished on the wiki holdout set, want eyes @matt @julia

matt: nice, rough numbers?

joulia: oops typo — julia: can you paste the eval command and index config?

zoe: recall@10 dropped ~2.3% when we switched to naive int8 quant (one-shot dynamic). float32 baseline: 0.742 recall@10, int8 (naive): 0.719. silhouette went from 0.34 -> 0.28.

matt: hmm that magnitude is material. did you use per-channel quant or per-tensor?

zoe: per-tensor first pass. index: HNSW ef_search=128, M=16, PQ disabled. distance=cosine.

ryan: can you try per-channel and asymmetric quant? sometimes that helps embeddings with wide activation ranges.

zoe: yep scheduled. running per-channel int8 + small calibration set (5k samples) now.

julia: also check embedding norm distribution — int8 can clamp tails. a tiny postnorm tweak sometimes recovers recall.

zoe: good call. posted the quick eval snippet below:

```
# eval quick-run
python eval_embeddings.py \
  --model sablefish-embed-v1 \
  --quant int8-perchannel \
  --calib-samples 5000 \
  --index hnsw --ef 128 --M 16 \
  --dist cosine --holdout wiki_holdout.jsonl
```

zoe: intermediate results: int8-perchannel recall@10 = 0.735, silhouette = 0.31. variance across seeds higher (std ~0.007) vs float32 (std ~0.002). latency per-embed dropped ~38%.

anya: tradeoff looks plausible. any language-specific regressions?

zoe: yes — en and fr stable, ja saw biggest drop (recall@10 -0.045). likely tokenization / sequence-length skew.

matt: can we try keeping text-normalization the same but force float16 on the Transformer matmuls only? (hybrid fp16 + int8 KV cache)

zoe: will run hybrid fp16 main path + int8 KV cache next. also going to try L2 distance instead of cosine as a sanity check.

ci-bot: nightly-eval job #sablefish-2026-03-21 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/sablefish/6111112222/ (metrics.json, tsne.png)

zoe: grabbed tsne — clusters look more jumbled in naive int8, per-channel looks closer to float32. attaching quickfp: tsne link in artifacts.

julia: thanks. can you add a small holdout of short queries (<8 tokens) vs long (>128) — we saw short-query fragility on other onboards.

zoe: added short/long split to the next run. plan: promote float16 as default in staging, keep int8-perchannel experiments in canary with stricter monitoring (recall delta alert at 1.5% absolute).

matt: agree. please file a short PR with the evaluation commands and the per-lang results table so we can review before promote.

zoe: will do — PR incoming, ETA ~2 hours. :white_check_mark:

anya: nice work — document the tokenization diffs for ja, that might help future model adapters.

zoe: noted. follow-ups: (1) per-channel int8 sweep with different calib sets, (2) hybrid fp16+int8 experiment, (3) short/long query sensitivity check. I'll post results in this thread.

matt: ping when PR is up.

zoe: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/842 — includes metrics table + quick reproducible script

julia: got it, starting review now.

zoe: final quick note — recommendation for product: promote sablefish-embed-v1 as float16 for Hosted and Dedicated; keep int8-perchannel as opt-in for Dedicated only until we shrink per-lang variance.

matt: SGTM

ci-bot: label: "eval-ready" added to PR #842 by zoe
